why: Quest asked for construction materials on the front page and has no photography of its own of them — Quest photographs jobs, not stock. These are the only photographs on the site Quest did not take.
rule: CC0 only. Public-domain dedication: commercial use permitted, no attribution required, no share-alike. Anything added here must carry the same, and build/lib/images.test.mjs enforces that every non-Quest image in the tree is listed in this file.

rejected.why: Terracotta roof tiles with KERALA TILES and JOHN'S TILE WORKS cast into their faces. Another firm's name on Quest's front page, which is the same rule that ruled out six of the seven machine cut-outs in assets/cut/.

retired.why: Removed from the tree, not merely unreferenced. It existed only to be the ground under the old hero's accent plane, and that plane is gone: the front page is a full-bleed photograph of a Quest jobsite now, on the same construction as every other page's banner. Nothing else ever used it.
retired.rule: This file must stay out of assets/. It is CC0 and there was never anything wrong with it — there is simply nothing left for it to be the ground of. images.test.mjs fails if it reappears.

images.rights: cc0, wikimedia — fine to have used, simply no longer needed.

supplied.why: Files Quest supplied directly (dropped into Downloads and named by file, not by source). They are used as given.
supplied.rights: NOT VERIFIED HERE. This did not come through the CC0 search the images list above went through, and it carries no licence metadata of its own — it looks like commercial stock. If it came from a paid stock licence that covers commercial use, nothing more is needed. If it did not, it needs replacing before this is a problem: the site is a trading contractor’s, so "found on the internet" is not a licence. Raised with Quest three times, including once when it was removed from the tree entirely and once when Quest asked for it back. Using it is Quest’s call and the rights are Quest’s to hold.

images.note: Arrived already matted — 2000x2000 with a real alpha channel, 70% of it transparent — so it needed only trimming to its subject and re-encoding. No background removal was done here.

placeholders.why: Quest asked for photographs on the service pages for trades its own library does not cover, and asked for them to be marked in the code as stock that will be replaced. These are those. They are openly licensed photographs of other people's jobs, they sit under assets/stock/ rather than assets/quest/, and none of them is in the gallery — the gallery is presented as Quest's own completed work and a stock frame in there would be a claim about a job Quest did not do.
placeholders.status: TO BE REPLACED. Every file here is a placeholder for a photograph Quest has not taken yet. When Quest supplies its own frame for a trade, the placeholder for that trade comes out of the tree, not just out of the pool.
placeholders.rule: Unlike the CC0 list above, these are NOT attribution-free. 16 of the 20 carry a CC BY or CC BY-SA licence and REQUIRE a visible credit wherever they are published. The site carries no credit line today, so either a credits page goes up carrying the credit_line of every attribution_required file below, or those files come out. build/lib/images.test.mjs holds this block to the same standard as the rest: every file listed must be in the tree, must carry its licence and its credit line, and must not describe itself as a Quest job.
placeholders.share_alike: Several are CC BY-SA. Publishing the photograph on a page does not put the page under that licence, but publishing a modified version of the photograph does. These were resized and re-encoded only, which is not an adaptation. Do not crop, recolour or composite them without checking the licence on the file first.
